glosses.notes: Imported from the source PDF. The source marks this entry as verb.

examples.sentence: 这本旧书刚拿起来就散了，所以老师先让我们轻一点翻，免得里面那几张图也跟着掉出来。
风一大，门口刚放好的纸又被吹散了，所以他们只好蹲在地上重新一张一张排好，免得后面的人拿错。
母亲把几张照片散在床上，让孩子一边看一边找去年那张，因为放在手机里时大家总是认不出来。

example_translations.translation: This old book fell apart as soon as it was picked up, so the teacher first told us to turn the pages more gently so that the pictures inside would not fall out too.

When the wind picked up, the papers that had just been set by the door were blown all over again, so they had to squat on the ground and arrange them one by one to keep the people coming later from taking the wrong ones.

My mother spread several photos out on the bed and had the child look for the one from last year while looking through them, because when they were kept on the phone, everyone kept failing to recognize it.

glosses.notes: Imported from the source PDF. The source marks this entry as noun.

examples.sentence: 老师说，读散文不能只看字面上的意思，还要看作者为什么明明写的是小事，最后却让人想到自己的生活。
她写的第一篇散文没有多讲大道理，只是把母亲早上做饭的样子慢慢写出来，结果很多人看完以后都安静了很久。
父亲以前不太喜欢散文，总觉得它不像故事那样有结果，后来才发现，有些散文写的正是人最难说清楚的感受。

example_translations.translation: The teacher said that when reading prose, you cannot look only at the literal meaning of the words. You also have to see why the writer is clearly describing small things yet in the end makes people think about their own lives.

The first piece of prose she wrote did not spend much time talking about big principles. It simply described her mother cooking in the morning bit by bit, and as a result many people stayed quiet for a long time after reading it.

My father did not like prose very much before and always felt it did not have a result the way stories do. Only later did he realize that some prose is writing exactly about the feelings people find hardest to explain clearly.

glosses.notes: Imported from the source PDF. The source marks this entry as verb.

examples.sentence: 会一结束，原来站在门口的人就慢慢散了，不过还有几个人没有马上走，而是留下来继续把最后的问题问清楚。
雨刚小一点，路边等车的人就开始散了，因为大家都怕再晚一会儿，后面的车会越来越难等。
老师本来想再多说两句，可是看到下课时间到了，教室后面的学生已经快散了，就先让大家回去休息。

example_translations.translation: As soon as the meeting ended, the people standing by the door slowly dispersed, though a few did not leave right away and stayed behind to keep asking about the last questions until they were clear.

As soon as the rain eased a little, the people waiting by the roadside started to disperse, because everyone was afraid that if they waited any longer, the later buses would become harder and harder to catch.

The teacher had wanted to say a little more, but when it was clear that class time was over and the students in the back of the room were already starting to break up, the teacher first let everyone go back and rest.

glosses.notes: Imported from the source PDF. The source marks this entry as verb.

examples.sentence: 这家店一到下午就会散发出面包刚出来的香味，所以很多路过的人明明不饿，也会先进去看一眼。
刚出锅的面一直散发出很香的味，所以站在门口等的人明明还没有点，也都先看了过来。
这杯热茶一直散发出香味，所以本来还在门外等的人也跟着走进来坐下了。

example_translations.translation: Every afternoon, this shop gives off the smell of bread just out of the oven, so many people passing by go in for a look even when they are not actually hungry.
The noodles that had just come out of the pot kept giving off a delicious smell, so even the people waiting at the door who had not ordered yet all looked over first.
This cup of hot tea kept giving off a pleasant fragrance, so even the people who had still been waiting outside the door came in and sat down too.

glosses.notes: Imported from the source PDF. The source marks this entry as noun.

examples.sentence: 他这几天一直跟客人说话，到了晚上才发现嗓子很疼，所以回家以后先喝了水，再决定第二天少说一点。
医生说，如果嗓子已经开始疼，就不要再一直吃太热或者太辣的东西，不然第二天更难开口说话。
母亲本来只是有点咳，可是后来嗓子越来越疼，那天连平常最简单的话，也要停几次才说完。

example_translations.translation: He had been talking with customers for the past few days, and only in the evening did he realize that his throat hurt badly, so after getting home he drank some water first and then decided to talk less the next day.
The doctor said that if your throat has already started to hurt, you should stop eating food that is too hot or too spicy all the time, or it will be even harder to speak the next day.
At first my mother only had a slight cough, but later her throat hurt more and more, and that day even the simplest things she normally said had to be finished with several pauses.

glosses.notes: Imported from the source PDF. The source marks this entry as verb.

examples.sentence: 人如果在一次又一次的失败以后丧失了继续学下去的信心，后面就算老师再有办法，也很难真的帮到他。
医生提醒他，手一旦丧失正常活动的能力，后面就算不太疼了，生活里很多小事还是会很不方便。
如果一家公司在最忙的时候丧失了大家之间最基本的信任，后面就算钱和人都够，很多事还是做不起来。

example_translations.translation: If a person loses the confidence to keep studying after one failure after another, then even if the teacher has good methods later, it is still hard to truly help that person.
The doctor reminded him that once a hand loses the ability to move normally, then even if it does not hurt much later, many small things in daily life will still become very inconvenient.
If a company loses the most basic trust among its people at its busiest moment, then even if it later has enough money and staff, many things still cannot be carried through.

glosses.notes: Imported from the source PDF. The source marks this entry as verb.

examples.sentence: 工作人员先把每个人带来的资料扫描进电脑，然后才按名字一份一份放好，这样后面有人要找的时候就快多了。
老师说，读文章不要只会扫描一遍，看到重要的地方还是要停下来想一想，不然后面的意思很容易接不上。
工作人员把旧照片一张一张扫描进电脑以后，又按时间放好，这样家里的人以后想找的时候就容易多了。

example_translations.translation: The staff first scanned the materials each person had brought into the computer and only then put them away one by one by name, so it became much faster when someone needed to find them later.

The teacher said that when reading an article, you should not just scan it once. When you come to an important part, you still need to stop and think about it, or the meaning that follows is easy to lose track of.
After the staff scanned the old photos into the computer one by one, they put them back in order by time, so it became much easier for the family to find them later.

glosses.notes: Imported from the source PDF. The source marks this entry as verb.

examples.sentence: 村里的人都知道，不能为了省事就把山上的小动物都杀掉，因为少了一种，别的东西也会慢慢变多。
父亲杀鱼的时候总让我站远一点，不是怕我帮不上忙，而是怕地上太滑，我一着急就会碰到旁边的刀。
过年以前，家里的人先在院子里杀鸡，然后母亲再把要用的东西一件一件拿进厨房。

example_translations.translation: People in the village all know that you cannot kill all the small animals in the hills just to save trouble, because once one kind becomes fewer, other things will slowly increase too.

When my father kills fish, he always tells me to stand farther away, not because he thinks I cannot help, but because the ground is too slippery and if I get nervous, I might hit the knife beside him.
Before the new year, the family first kills chickens in the yard, and then my mother brings the things that will be needed into the kitchen one by one.

glosses.notes: Imported from the source PDF. The source marks this entry as verb, noun.

examples.sentence: 司机开到学校门口的时候先轻轻刹车，因为前面刚有两个孩子跑过去，他怕自己看见得太晚会来不及停。
这条路一下雨就很滑，所以父亲每次下坡以前都会先试一下刹车，确定没有问题才继续往前开。
后面的车离得太近的时候，最怕前面的车突然刹车，所以教练一直提醒我们开车时不要只顾着看眼前一点。

example_translations.translation: As the driver reached the school gate, the driver braked lightly first because two children had just run across in front, and the driver was afraid that if they were seen too late, there would not be time to stop.
This road becomes very slippery as soon as it rains, so every time before going downhill, my father tests the brake first and only keeps driving once he is sure there is no problem.
When the car behind is too close, what people fear most is the car in front braking suddenly, so the driving coach keeps reminding us not to focus only on one small point ahead while driving.

glosses.notes: Imported from the source PDF. The source marks this entry as noun.

examples.sentence: 孩子第一次看到鲨鱼的时候，先紧张得一直抓着母亲的手，后来发现前面有很厚的玻璃，才慢慢敢走近一点看。
老师放那段海里的片子时特别提醒我们，别一看到鲨鱼就只想到可怕，因为它在海里的位置其实很重要。
导游说，那条鲨鱼虽然看起来很大，可是它一直在玻璃后面慢慢游，所以大家不用往后退得那么快。

example_translations.translation: When the child saw a shark for the first time, the child got so nervous that the child kept holding tightly to the mother’s hand. Only after noticing the thick glass in front did the child slowly dare to move a little closer.
When the teacher showed that film clip from the sea, the teacher especially reminded us not to think only of fear whenever we see a shark, because its place in the sea is actually very important.
The guide said that although that shark looked very large, it was swimming slowly behind the glass the whole time, so everyone did not need to step back so quickly.

glosses.notes: Imported from the source PDF. The source marks this entry as verb.

examples.sentence: 公司收到的材料太多，所以第一步只能先筛选出真正符合条件的人，不然后面的时间根本来不及安排。
老师说，信息太多的时候，最重要的不是全部记住，而是先学会筛选出对自己现在最有用的部分。
医生把检查结果都放在一起看了一遍，先筛选出最要紧的几项，再一点一点向家里解释后面的情况。

example_translations.translation: The company received too many materials, so in the first step it could only screen out the people who truly met the requirements; otherwise there would simply not be enough time to arrange the later stages.
The teacher said that when there is too much information, what matters most is not remembering all of it, but first learning how to filter out the parts that are most useful for you right now.
The doctor looked through all the test results together and first screened out the few items that mattered most, then explained the later situation to the family bit by bit.

glosses.notes: Imported from the source PDF. The source marks this entry as noun.

examples.sentence: 我们快到山顶的时候风已经很大了，可是前面的人还是没有停，因为大家都想在天黑以前看一眼最远的地方。
老人年轻时常一个人走到山顶去坐一会儿，他说不是为了证明自己多能走，而是那里真的很安静。
雨过以后，山顶上面还有一点白雾没有散开，所以站在下面看的人都觉得那条路像通到天里一样。

example_translations.translation: By the time we were almost at the mountaintop, the wind was already very strong, but the people ahead still did not stop because everyone wanted to see the farthest point before it got dark.
When he was young, the old man often walked to the mountaintop and sat there for a while by himself. He said it was not to prove how far he could walk, but because it was truly quiet there.
After the rain passed, a little white mist still had not cleared from above the mountaintop, so the people standing below all felt that the path looked as if it led right up into the sky.

glosses.notes: Imported from the source PDF. The source marks this entry as noun.

examples.sentence: 车过桥以后，远处那座山峰就慢慢清楚起来了，孩子一直把脸贴在窗上看，生怕一转弯就看不见了。
老师拿着地图给大家讲的时候，说那座最高的山峰虽然看上去离得不远，可是真走过去要花很长时间。
太阳快下去的时候，最后一点光正好落在山峰上，所以原来坐着不说话的人也都拿出手机想拍下来。

example_translations.translation: After the car crossed the bridge, that mountain peak in the distance slowly became clear. The child kept pressing the child’s face to the window, afraid it would disappear as soon as the road turned.
While holding the map and explaining things to everyone, the teacher said that although the highest mountain peak looked not very far away, actually walking there would take a very long time.
When the sun was about to go down, the last bit of light fell exactly on the mountain peak, so even the people who had been sitting quietly pulled out their phones to take a picture.

glosses.notes: Imported from the source PDF. The source marks this entry as noun.

examples.sentence: 雨一停，孩子们就想往山坡下面跑，老师只好先把他们叫住，因为地上还是很滑，一不小心就会坐到地上。
老人年轻时在那个山坡上种过很多树，所以后来再回去看的时候，一眼就能认出哪几棵是自己种的。
车开到山坡边上的小路时，父亲让大家先下车走一段，因为再往前开的话，一旦打滑就不好回头了。

example_translations.translation: As soon as the rain stopped, the children wanted to run down the mountainside, so the teacher had to stop them first because the ground was still slippery and they could easily fall to the ground if they were not careful.
When he was young, the old man planted many trees on that mountain slope, so when he later went back to look, he could recognize at a glance which ones he had planted himself.

When the car reached the small road by the mountain slope, my father told everyone to get out and walk part of the way first, because if they kept driving and the car started to slip, it would be hard to turn back.

glosses.notes: Imported from the source PDF. The source marks this entry as verb.

examples.sentence: 门一打开，外面的光突然往里一闪，坐在里面的人都先抬起头看了一眼，还以为是谁这么早就来了。
她刚说到最重要的地方，电脑屏幕突然闪了一下，大家一下都安静了，因为谁都怕刚写好的东西没有了。
远处的玻璃在太阳下面一闪，司机马上把速度放慢，因为那一瞬间他差一点没有看清前面的路。

example_translations.translation: As soon as the door opened, the light outside flashed inward, and the people sitting inside all looked up first, thinking someone had arrived so early.

Just as she was getting to the most important point, the computer screen flashed once, and everyone suddenly went quiet because each person was afraid that the work that had just been written might be gone.
The glass in the distance flashed in the sunlight, and the driver immediately slowed down, because for that brief moment the driver almost could not see the road ahead clearly.

glosses.notes: Imported from the source PDF. The source marks this entry as noun.

examples.sentence: 半夜里窗外突然一道闪电过去，孩子一下从床上坐了起来，后来听见父亲说不要怕，才慢慢又躺下。
山里一有闪电，大家就不要再往高的地方走了，先找个安全的地方等一等才更重要。
外面先是一道闪电过去，后来风也越来越大，所以父亲马上起身去把还开着的窗关好了。

example_translations.translation: In the middle of the night, a flash of lightning suddenly went across outside the window, and the child sat up in bed at once. Only after hearing the father say not to be afraid did the child slowly lie down again.
As soon as there is lightning in the mountains, everyone should stop going toward higher ground. Finding a safe place and waiting first is more important.
Outside, a flash of lightning came first, and then the wind grew stronger and stronger, so my father immediately got up and shut the window that was still open.

glosses.notes: Measure word used with doors and windows.

examples.sentence: 这扇门一到下雨天就不好开，所以父亲前几天刚找人来看过，可是到现在也没有完全修好。
她坐在靠窗的位置，旁边那扇窗一打开，外面的风就一直往里进，所以纸上的角总是往上翻。
教室后面有两扇很大的窗，太阳一出来，里面一下就亮了很多，所以大家早上常常不用马上开灯。

example_translations.translation: This door is hard to open as soon as it rains, so my father had just asked someone to come look at it a few days ago, but even now it still has not been completely repaired.
She was sitting by the window, and as soon as that window beside her was opened, the wind outside kept blowing in, so the corners of the papers kept turning upward.

There are two very large windows at the back of the classroom, and as soon as the sun comes out, the room becomes much brighter, so in the morning people often do not need to switch on the lights right away.

glosses.notes: Imported from the source PDF. The source marks this entry as noun.

examples.sentence: 老板说，一个好名字还不够，如果没有早点把商标办好，后面东西卖得再好，也可能被别人先拿去用。
孩子原来只觉得那个商标好看，后来听母亲慢慢解释以后，才知道一个小小的图为什么能让人一下认出是哪家公司。
公司这次换商标，不是为了突然显得更新，而是因为原来的那个样子放到手机上以后，很多细节都看不清了。

example_translations.translation: The owner said that having a good name is not enough. If the trademark is not handled early, then even if the product sells well later, someone else may get to use it first.

At first the child only thought that trademark looked nice, but after listening to the mother explain it slowly, the child understood why one small image could make people recognize which company it belonged to at once.
This time the company changed its trademark not to suddenly look newer, but because when the old one was shown on a phone, many details could no longer be seen clearly.

glosses.notes: Source seed row appears malformed; headword normalized to 伤口 to match the pronunciation and gloss.

examples.sentence: 医生说，这个伤口虽然不算深，可是这几天还是不要碰水，不然外面刚长好的地方很容易又开。
孩子跑的时候摔了一下，腿上出了一个伤口，母亲先让他坐下，再一点一点把上面的土洗干净。
护士换药的时候提醒家里的人，如果伤口开始发红或者一直疼，就不要再自己等了，最好马上回来看看。

example_translations.translation: The doctor said that although this wound is not especially deep, it should still not be touched with water for the next few days, or the place that has just started to heal may open again easily.
The child fell while running and got a wound on the leg. The mother first had the child sit down and then slowly washed the dirt off it.
While changing the medicine, the nurse reminded the family that if the wound started turning red or kept hurting, they should stop waiting on their own and come back to have it checked right away.

glosses.notes: Imported from the source PDF. The source marks this entry as verb, noun.

examples.sentence: 这次事故发生得很快，不过因为前面的人先把大家叫开了，所以最后没有造成大的伤亡，这已经很不容易了。
老师看新闻的时候总提醒我们，看到伤亡数字先不要只觉得远，因为每一个数字后面其实都是一个家。
救援的人赶到以后，第一件事不是马上搬东西，而是先确认还有没有新的伤亡，不然越忙越容易乱。

example_translations.translation: This accident happened very quickly, but because the people in front had already called everyone away, it did not end up causing major casualties, and that was already not easy.
Whenever the teacher watches the news, the teacher reminds us not to feel that casualty numbers are far away from us, because behind every number there is actually a family.

After the rescue team arrived, the first thing they did was not to start moving things immediately, but to confirm first whether there were any new casualties, because the busier people get, the easier it is for things to become chaotic.

glosses.notes: Imported from the source PDF. The source marks this entry as noun.

examples.sentence: 医生先看了最安静的那个伤员，因为有时候越不喊疼的人，情况反而越需要马上处理。
车一停下，几个人就一起把伤员小心抬下来，然后直接送进里面已经准备好的地方做检查。
护士后来告诉家里的人，照顾伤员的时候最重要的不是一直围在旁边，而是按医生说的时间一步一步来。

example_translations.translation: The doctor saw the quietest wounded person first, because sometimes the people who do not cry out in pain are actually the ones whose condition most needs to be handled immediately.
As soon as the vehicle stopped, several people carefully lifted the wounded person down together and then took the person directly inside to the place that had already been prepared for examination.
Later the nurse told the family that when caring for a wounded person, the most important thing is not to keep crowding around, but to follow the doctor’s timing step by step.

glosses.notes: Imported from the source PDF. The source marks this entry as verb.

examples.sentence: 老人最怕接到那种很急的电话，因为人一着急就容易上当，连平时明明知道该先问清楚的话都忘了。
她回家以后才知道自己上当了，所以先把那条消息又看了一遍，然后才给朋友打电话问该怎么办。
老师提醒我们，看到太便宜的东西不要马上交钱，不是说一定有问题，而是太着急的人最容易上当。

example_translations.translation: What older people fear most is getting that kind of urgent phone call, because once a person gets anxious, it becomes easy to be tricked, and even the questions they clearly know they should ask first get forgotten.
Only after she got home did she realize that she had been tricked, so she read that message over once more first and only then called a friend to ask what she should do.

The teacher reminded us not to hand over money immediately when we see something that is too cheap. It is not that there must be a problem, but that people who get too anxious are the easiest to trick.

glosses.notes: Imported from the source PDF. The source marks this entry as noun.

examples.sentence: 他把最前面的情况先写清楚，才送给上级去看，因为如果只是口头说一遍，很多细节过两天就容易忘。
医院临时多来了这么多人以后，值班的人先向上级说明情况，然后才决定后面的房间和人要怎么分。
父亲年轻时最怕见上级，总觉得一开口就会说错话，后来才明白，对方最在意的其实是你有没有把事情准备好。

example_translations.translation: He first wrote out the situation at the front clearly before sending it to his superior, because if he only explained it once by word of mouth, many details would easily be forgotten after a couple of days.

After so many extra people suddenly arrived at the hospital, the staff member on duty first explained the situation to the higher-level office and only then decided how the later rooms and people should be divided.

When my father was young, he was most afraid of meeting his superiors and always felt that he would say something wrong as soon as he opened his mouth. Only later did he understand that what they actually care about most is whether you have prepared the matter properly.

glosses.notes: Imported from the source PDF. The source marks this entry as verb.

examples.sentence: 父亲常说，人想上进，不是每天只说大话，而是该做的小事今天就先认真做好，不要总等明天。
她刚来公司的时候经验不多，可是人很上进，别人下班以后她还会把白天没听懂的地方自己再看一遍。
老师最怕的不是学生慢，而是明明很上进，却因为总被人拿来比较，后来连开口都不太敢了。

example_translations.translation: My father often says that if a person wants to make progress, it is not about talking big every day, but about seriously doing today’s small tasks first instead of always waiting for tomorrow.

When she first came to the company, she did not have much experience, but she was eager to improve herself. After other people got off work, she still reviewed the parts from the day that she had not understood.

What the teacher fears most is not that students are slow, but that someone is clearly trying hard to improve and yet, because the person is always being compared with others, later does not even dare to speak much.

glosses.notes: Imported from the source PDF. The source marks this entry as verb.

examples.sentence: 这家公司为了准备上市，先把前几年的材料都按时间重新放好，这样有人来问的时候，马上就能找到。
新书一上市，门口就来了很多想买的人，所以老板后来只好临时再从后面拿一些出来，才够当天卖。
老板说，东西能不能马上上市，不只是看外面是不是已经做好，还要看后面的人能不能一直跟得上。

example_translations.translation: To prepare to go public, this company first put all the materials from the previous years back in order by time, so that whenever someone came to ask about them, they could be found right away.

As soon as the new book came onto the market, many people came to the door wanting to buy it, so the owner later had no choice but to bring out more from the back temporarily before there was enough to sell that day.
The boss said that whether something can be launched right away does not depend only on whether the outside part is already ready, but also on whether the people behind it can keep up the whole time.
